record.context_brief: Structure of minimal 4-centerpole sets in R4
record.original_question: Call a subset C ⊂ R^4 4-centerpole when the central symmetries with centers in C force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset under every 4-coloring. Is every 12-element 4-centerpole subset of R^4 affinely equivalent to the sandwich Ξ^3_1, the 12-point subset of Z^4 whose slices {-1} × 2^3_{<1}, {0} × 2^3_{<3}, and {1} × 2^3_{>1} have 1, 7, and 4 points, respectively?

evidence.quote: We shall say that a subset C ⊂ Rn is r-centerpole if the family of central symmetries SC = {sc : c ∈ C} is (r, 0)-centerpole, which means that msr(Rn, asdim, SC ) ≥ 0.
• Ξ31 is a 12-element subset of Z4 whose slices {−1} × 23−1, {0} × 23<3 and {1} × 23>1 have 1, 7 and 4 points, respectively.
Problem 10.6. Is each 12-element 4-centerpole set in R4 affinely equivalent to the 31-sandwich Ξ31?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the central symmetry centered at $c$ is the map $s_c : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ defined by $s_c(x) = 2c - x$. A subset $S \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called symmetric (with respect to some $c$) if $s_c(S) = S$. Given a positive integer $r$, call a subset $C \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ an $r$-centerpole set if, for every coloring $\chi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$, there exist a color $i$, a center $c \in C$, and an unbounded subset $S \subset \chi^{-1}(i)$ with $s_c(S) = S$.

For positive integers $k \le n$, let $2^n_{<k} = \{(x_1,\dots,x_n) \in \{0,1\}^n : x_1 + \cdots + x_n < k\}$ and similarly $2^n_{>k}$, $2^n_{\le k}$, $2^n_{\ge k}$. Define the "$3_1$-sandwich"
$$\Xi^3_1 \subset \mathbb{Z}^4$$
to be the $12$-point set whose slices satisfy
$$\Xi^3_1 \cap (\{-1\} \times \mathbb{Z}^3) = \{-1\} \times 2^3_{\le 1},\quad \Xi^3_1 \cap (\{0\} \times \mathbb{Z}^3) = \{0\} \times 2^3_{<3},\quad \Xi^3_1 \cap (\{1\} \times \mathbb{Z}^3) = \{1\} \times 2^3_{>1},$$
i.e., the slice over $-1$ has $1$ point, the slice over $0$ has $7$ points, and the slice over $1$ has $4$ points (totalling $12$ points).

Two subsets $A, B \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ are affinely equivalent if there is an invertible affine map $\mathbb{R}^4 \to \mathbb{R}^4$ taking $A$ onto $B$.

Question: Is every $12$-element $4$-centerpole subset of $\mathbb{R}^4$ affinely equivalent to $\Xi^3_1$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on centerpole sets in Abelian groups and Ramsey-type theorems for symmetric monochromatic subsets (e.g., arXiv:1003.2588 and the Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets paper on Ramsey treatments of symmetry), but no source directly resolving the specific classification question for 12-element 4-centerpole sets in $\mathbb{R}^4$ as affine images of $\Xi^3_1$ was found. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Centerpole sets for colorings of Abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Defines k-centerpole subsets and studies cardinal characteristics c_k(G) for colorings of groups G.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of centerpole sets and the framework relevant to this question is established but no resolution of the 12-point R^4 case is given here.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monochromatic symmetric subsets under finite colorings.
status_evidence.claim: Background framework on monochromatic symmetric subsets; does not resolve the affine-equivalence question for 12-element 4-centerpole sets in R^4.
